entries.title: Node.js child_process command construction from untrusted input
source_cues: HTTP/RPC/message values flow into command arguments
TypeScript values cross erased type annotations or JavaScript interop
sink_cues: node:child_process exec/execSync command string
execFile/spawn options including shell, argv, and executable path
language_pitfalls: exec and execSync invoke a shell; string concatenation and interpolation can enable command injection.
execFile/spawn are safer only when shell execution is disabled and untrusted data remains a separate argument.
Type annotations do not validate runtime input; validate deserialized and any-typed values.
Type annotations are erased at runtime; external values require runtime validation.
counterevidence: Only a fixed executable is invoked with a fixed argv structure, shell:false, and validated values.
verification_steps: Trace untrusted values to child_process APIs and identify the exact API/overload/options.
Verify shell behavior, argument boundaries, executable selection, and platform-specific quoting.
Use a harmless sentinel command in an isolated harness and compare an argv-based negative control.

entries.title: Dynamic code evaluation from untrusted TypeScript runtime values
source_cues: untrusted data reaches an evaluation or module-loading input
generated JavaScript runtime values bypass static TypeScript types
sink_cues: eval and Function constructors
node:vm runIn* APIs and dynamic code-generation APIs
language_pitfalls: Dynamic import of a fixed module is not equivalent to evaluating attacker-controlled source.
Template construction and transpilation can create an execution sink even when the input is typed as string.
Type annotations are erased at runtime; external values require runtime validation.
counterevidence: Only fixed reviewed source is evaluated and untrusted input remains data.
verification_steps: Trace attacker-controlled bytes through decoding, templating, and code generation to the evaluator.
Distinguish data arguments from source text and inspect sandbox/realm boundaries.
Use a harmless expression sentinel and a non-evaluating control.

entries.title: Unbounded Node.js stream or request-body accumulation
source_cues: remote request or stream chunks are appended to persistent buffers/arrays
multiple consumers or retries retain chunks beyond request lifetime
sink_cues: Readable/data event accumulation and Buffer.concat
body parsers, message queues, and per-request chunk arrays
language_pitfalls: A stream API does not imply backpressure is enabled.
Count and byte limits must be applied before retaining each chunk; per-request limits may still permit aggregate exhaustion.
Type annotations are erased at runtime; external values require runtime validation.
counterevidence: A byte/count cap is enforced before append and overflow terminates or backpressures the producer.
verification_steps: Trace chunk production, buffering, consumption, cancellation, and cleanup.
Measure retained bytes under bounded and over-limit streams with a negative control.
Check per-connection and aggregate concurrency limits.

entries.title: Missing authorization on a TypeScript service operation
source_cues: authenticated or anonymous request reaches a state-changing handler
route parameter selects a protected object
sink_cues: Express/Koa/Fastify route handlers and service methods
database writes, secret reads, and administrative operations
language_pitfalls: Authentication middleware does not prove object- or action-level authorization.
Decorator/type declarations do not enforce runtime authorization unless middleware is wired on every route.
Type annotations are erased at runtime; external values require runtime validation.
counterevidence: A verified authorization policy dominates the operation for every registered route and alias.
verification_steps: Enumerate route registration, middleware ordering, aliases, and service entry points.
Test anonymous, low-privilege, owner, and cross-tenant principals.

entries.title: Unbounded queues, timers, retries, or object retention in a TypeScript runtime
source_cues: attacker-controlled requests schedule retained work or objects
queue growth outpaces bounded consumers
sink_cues: arrays/maps/queues, timers, promises, worker queues, and buffered streams
retained closures/listeners and retry scheduling
language_pitfalls: Garbage collection does not reclaim objects reachable from queues, listeners, timers, or caches.
Per-item limits do not bound aggregate concurrency or retry amplification.
Type annotations are erased at runtime; external values require runtime validation.
counterevidence: Queue, concurrency, retention, and retry budgets are enforced before admitting work and on failure paths.
verification_steps: Identify the retaining owner and every enqueue, retry, cancellation, and drain transition.
Measure queue depth and retained memory with bounded and adversarial-rate controls.

entries.title: Broken object-level authorization through a user-controlled TypeScript key
source_cues: route/body/query identifier selects a database object
tenant or owner identity is available separately from the selected key
sink_cues: ORM findById/findUnique and repository lookups
filesystem/object-store keys and cache entries selected by request parameters
language_pitfalls: UUIDs and unguessable identifiers do not replace authorization.
TypeScript DTO types do not establish ownership or tenant membership at runtime.
Type annotations are erased at runtime; external values require runtime validation.
counterevidence: The query is scoped by the authenticated principal/tenant or an equivalent policy is checked before use.
verification_steps: Trace request-controlled identifiers to reads and writes, including batch and nested routes.
Compare owner, same-tenant, and cross-tenant access outcomes.

entries.title: Unsafe cryptographic algorithm or parameter selection in a TypeScript runtime
source_cues: request/config values select algorithm, digest, key, IV, or mode
serialized keys/parameters cross a runtime trust boundary
sink_cues: node:crypto createCipheriv/createDecipheriv/createSign/createVerify
WebCrypto subtle.importKey/sign/verify algorithm dictionaries
language_pitfalls: Runtime algorithm strings require an explicit allowlist and compatible parameter checks.
A successful API call does not establish safe key size, mode, nonce handling, or protocol binding.
Type annotations are erased at runtime; external values require runtime validation.
counterevidence: Algorithm and parameter choices are fixed or allowlisted with validated key/nonce constraints.
verification_steps: Trace algorithm and parameter sources to the exact Node/WebCrypto primitive.
Check key length, mode, nonce uniqueness, tag verification, and error behavior.

entries.title: Untrusted data reaches an HTML or DOM execution sink
source_cues: request/API/storage data reaches browser-rendered markup
server template output is embedded into an HTML/JS context
sink_cues: DOM innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML/document.write
React dangerouslySetInnerHTML and unescaped server template output
language_pitfalls: Framework escaping is context-dependent; raw HTML escape hatches bypass it.
URL, script, attribute, and HTML-body contexts require different encoding rules.
Type annotations are erased at runtime; external values require runtime validation.
counterevidence: The framework uses context-correct escaping and no raw HTML sink receives attacker-controlled data.
verification_steps: Trace the value into the final browser/template context and inspect sanitization order.
Use a harmless markup sentinel and a context-matched encoded control.

entries.title: Cross-site request forgery against cookie-authenticated TypeScript endpoints
source_cues: browser-originated state change uses ambient cookies
cross-origin form/fetch reaches a mutation route
sink_cues: state-changing Express/Koa/Fastify routes
cookie-authenticated JSON/form endpoints and credentialed fetch handlers
language_pitfalls: CORS is not a general CSRF defense for form submissions or simple requests.
SameSite behavior depends on cookie attributes, browser context, and cross-site navigation.
Type annotations are erased at runtime; external values require runtime validation.
counterevidence: A verified anti-CSRF token/origin policy protects every state-changing cookie-authenticated route.
verification_steps: Map cookie attributes and route methods, then test cross-site form and credentialed fetch controls.
Check origin/referrer validation and token binding on aliases.

entries.title: Path traversal through TypeScript/Node filesystem operations
source_cues: request/archive/object key controls a filesystem path
base directory and user-controlled relative path are combined
sink_cues: node:fs open/readFile/writeFile/createReadStream/unlink
path.join/path.resolve results used for filesystem access
language_pitfalls: path.join is normalization, not a containment proof.
Check the resolved target against the intended root after normalization and account for symlinks.
Type annotations are erased at runtime; external values require runtime validation.
counterevidence: The canonical resolved path remains under the trusted root and symlink policy is enforced.
verification_steps: Trace path inputs through decoding, path.resolve, symlinks, and the final fs operation.
Test traversal encodings and symlink controls against an in-root negative case.
